thread:
maria (Perf): Quick sync — I'm seeing a perf divergence between A100 and H100 for long sequences (2k+). Autotuner seems to pick a tensor-core BF16 path on H100 but falls back on A100, throughput on A100 is ~20% lower for the same batch. Anyone else hit this?

liam (Runtime): Yep, saw traces this morning. The kernel selector uses reported SM/compute capability + capability flags, but after the driver roll some A100s were reporting BF16 support differently. Pasting what I collected from one node: 

```bash
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,compute_cap --format=csv
name, driver_version, compute_cap
A100-SXM4-40GB, 535.86, 8.0
H100-PCIe-80GB, 535.101, 9.0
```

liam (Runtime): And a quick device prop dump from CUDA probe: 

```python
# device probe snippet from runtime
props = cudaGetDeviceProperties(0)
print(props.major, props.minor)  # 8 0 for A100
print(props.multiProcessorCount)
# heuristics we use: sm = major*10 + minor -> 80 for A100, 90 for H100
```

olivia (ML): We turned on an FP8 experiment earlier — H100 takes advantage of the FP8 + tensor core path and shows big gains. A100 doesn't have the same FP8 hw path and needs different kernels. We need an explicit capability flag instead of inferring from SM only.

noah (Infra): FYI we rolled a driver (535.x) to some clusters last week. Some nodes still had 520.x and the probe results are inconsistent across the cluster. I'll patch infra metadata to include a stable capability tag so runtime doesn't rely on driver quirks.

perf-bot: [automated] perf-regression alert: model=redwood-neo-13b quant=bf16 cluster=eu-west-1-gpu-a100 throughput_drop=14% (compared to baseline 1710000000). See <https://dash.internal/perf/1710004321>.

maria (Perf): Proposed short-term autotuner rule: don't only check SM version. Check explicit capability flags: supports_bf16_tensor_ops, supports_fp8_accel, has_tensor_cores. Pseudocode: 

```text
if device.flags.supports_bf16_tensor_ops and device.sm >= 90:
    pick("tensor_core_bf16_kernels")
elif device.flags.supports_bf16_tensor_ops and device.sm >= 80:
    prefer("tensor_core_bf16") with fallback("amx_fp32")
else:
    pick("standard_matmul_kernels")
# also include seq-length pathing:
# if seq_len < 512 -> small-kernel, else -> large-kernel to reduce kernel-launch overhead
```

liam (Runtime): Addendum — sequence-length dependent paths are critical. For seq < 256 small tiling kernels win; for 256-2048 we prefer streaming-kernel with KV-chunking; for >2048 use chunked KV + lower-memory kernel. Also we saw that switching kernel mid-request can thrash the KV cache and cause evictions -> big perf cliffs.

maria (Perf): Good point about KV. We should add a guard: only switch kernels if estimated peak memory delta < 10% or if KV working set pinned. Pseudocode: 

```text
if will_change_kernel and (est_mem_delta_pct > 10 and not kv.pinned):
    keep_current_kernel()
else:
    apply_kernel_change()
```

olivia (ML): Can we also expose an override in deployment config so customers can force kernel-family (e.g., tensor_core_bf16|standard|fp8_experimental)? Some enterprise customers want deterministic behavior across mixed hardware.

noah (Infra): I'll add node labels: gpu.capabilities = ["bf16_tensor_ops","tensor_cores"] and driver.version metadata. Runtime can read these from instance metadata instead of probing drivers in some private deploys.

liam (Runtime): I'll open a PR for the autotuner: 
- add explicit capability flags read from probe + infra labels
- add seq-length thresholds in selector
- add KV-safe kernel switch guard

maria (Perf): Also add microbenchmarks: matmul kernels across SM versions + seq lengths to perf CI. Example matrix: SM=[70,80,90], seq=[64,256,1024,2048], batch=[1,4,8]. We need historical baselines so perf-bot can alert on regressions per-(sm,seq,batch) cell.

perf-bot: [automated] scheduled job created: perf-matrix-sm-seq-batch (runs nightly across labeled nodes).

liam (Runtime): One more note — drivers can misreport 'fp8' even if functional acceleration isn't available (emulation). We should treat fp8 flag as "opt-in" behind an env var until proven stable.

maria (Perf): Agreed. Short-term checklist:
- liam: PR for selector + KV guard
- olivia: add config override param + update docs
- noah: push node capability labels + roll driver fixes
- perf-bot: run nightly perf matrix and alert on >8% regression per cell

olivia (ML): I'll also add a test that emulates older SM by forcing capability flags in a container so CI can validate selector logic without having every HW type.

noah (Infra): 👍 tagging the 6 affected nodes now. Will post update once done.

maria (Perf): Thanks — I'll draft the PR and attach perf traces and CI matrix. Linking perf dashboard here: <https://dash.internal/perf/1710004321> :thumbsup:

liam (Runtime): Thanks — I'll coordinate review and block a canary rollout until we validate KV behavior.

maria (Perf): Closing thread for now. If you see new regressions ping me directly.
